subject: physics
title: Magnetism & Electromagnetism
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Magnetism & Electromagnetism from GCSE Physics.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics adventure on magnetic fields and electromagnetic induction.
final_note: You walked through fields, electromagnets and the motor effect.

concepts.def: Region around a magnet/current where a magnetic material feels a force; lines run N→S.
Permanent keeps its magnetism; induced is magnetic only in a field.
A coil carrying a current; stronger with more turns, current or an iron core.
A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field experiences a force (Fleming's left hand).
Moving a wire through a field induces a potential difference.
Changes the size of an alternating voltage using two coils on an iron core.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Magnets have north and south poles. Like poles repel; unlike attract.

Field lines go N -> S externally.

A current in a wire makes a magnetic field around it.

Coil it = solenoid: stronger, uniform field inside.

Add an iron core for an electromagnet.

A wire carrying current in a magnetic field experiences a force.

Use Fleming's left-hand rule for direction.

mcqs.q: Iron in a magnetic field becomes:
options: permanent magnet
induced magnet
non-magnetic
positively charged

mcqs.q: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of:
options: voltage
force on a current
field around a wire
induced emf

mcqs.q: What produces a magnetic field around a wire?
options: The metal in the wire is naturally magnetic.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
A moving electric charge — i.e. an electric current.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.

mcqs.q: What happens to the current as it goes around a series circuit?
options: It stays the same at every point — current is conserved.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
Current gets used up by each component as it flows around the circuit.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Solenoid”?
options: Region where force acts on magnet/current
Force on a current in a field
Coil of wire that acts like magnet
Always produces a field

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Permanent magnet”?
options: Coil of wire that acts like magnet
Always produces a field
Region where force acts on magnet/current
F, B, I directions

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Fleming's left hand”?
options: Magnetic only in a field
F, B, I directions
Force on a current in a field
Always produces a field

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Magnetic field”?
options: Force on a current in a field
Region where force acts on magnet/current
Always produces a field
Magnetic only in a field

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Motor effect”?
options: Always produces a field
Magnetic only in a field
Region where force acts on magnet/current
Force on a current in a field

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Induced magnet”?
options: Magnetic only in a field
F, B, I directions
Coil of wire that acts like magnet
Region where force acts on magnet/current
